questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code applies expiry to cached coverage results? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The payer API returns an error for a patient who has no cached entry. What does Check do, and what happens on the next call for the same patient?
choices: It caches an inactive coverage for 15 minutes and returns it
It returns a wrapped ErrPayerUnavailable and caches nothing, so the next call tries the payer again
It returns a wrapped ErrPayerUnavailable and caches the error for the default TTL
It returns Coverage{} with a nil error so scheduling can continue

questions.prompt: Why does Check store inactive coverage with a much shorter TTL than active coverage?
choices: A patient who renews or fixes their policy should be re-verified soon, while a stable active result can be trusted longer
The payer API rate limits inactive lookups
Inactive coverage cannot be serialized for long

questions.prompt: The context passed to StartSweeper is cancelled. What is the effect on the cache?
choices: The cache is cleared and Get returns false for every key
The cache panics on the next Get
The sweeper goroutine exits; the cache still works and expired entries are removed only when they are read
All entries are deleted by Sweep on the way out
